note: Adapted from Snyder's 1923 original English description; the original reads Anoplotermes parvus, new species; type alate male Cat. No. 26259, U.S.N.M.; type locality Frijoles, Canal Zone, Panama, 28 March 1923 (month 3), collected by W. M. Wheeler and I. Molino together with workers in a black-earth ant nest under a tree, with a first-form queen and a male in the same chamber. This genus has no soldier, and the original records only the alate. The same paper also describes Mirotermes panamaensis and Orthognathotermes wheeleri.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Darker and smaller than A. gracilis, which also occurs in Panama; the fontanelle lies closer to the posterior margin of the head than in gracilis, the postclypeus is shorter than in gracilis, the compound eyes are distinctly closer to the anterior margin of the head, and the pronotum is shorter than in gracilis. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 very short, only about half the length of segment 4, and segment 4 about half the length of segment 2. The queen and male are paler (nearer brown) than the alate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head greyish black, slightly longer than wide, widest at the compound eyes, wider than the pronotum, rounded posteriorly, densely covered with long hairs; fontanelle small, inconspicuous, a linear point in a depression. Postclypeus grey, nearly three times as wide as long, not much projecting, posterior margin deeply concave, with long hairs. Labrum yellow, ligulate, widest near the base, with long hairs, reaching the apex of the mandibles. Mandibles yellow chestnut brown at the apex, short. Compound eyes purple-black, large, projecting, very close to the lateral margin of the head, nearer the anterior margin. Ocelli large, elongate, upper margin projecting, less than their short diameter from the compound eyes, placed obliquely to the eyes. Antennae greyish brown, 15-segmented, hairy; segment 3 very small, half of segment 4; segment 4 half of segment 2; segments becoming wider and longer towards the apex; apical segment conical. Pronotum greyish brown, less than twice as wide as long, widest anteriorly, slightly semicircular, anterior and posterior margins nearly straight, with long hairs. Mesonotum and metanotum greyish brown, posterior margin concave, hairy. Wings dark, fringed with cilia, surface hairy; media of the forewing nearer the cubitus than the subcosta, branching near the apex; cubitus not reaching the wing apex, with 6 branches towards the posterior margin. Legs greyish brown, long, slender, hairy. Abdomen grey, densely covered with long hairs. Measurements (mm): alate total length 6.75—7.50; dealate total length 4.50—5.0; head length (to the apex of the labrum) 0.77—0.85; left mandible length 0.37; pronotum length 0.32—0.35; hind tibia length 0.70; forewing length 5.5—5.75; wing scale length 0.32; compound eye long diameter 0.17—0.20; head width (at the widest point) 0.65—0.70; pronotum width 0.60—0.65; forewing width 1.55; queen length 13.0, width 2.80.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality Frijoles, Canal Zone, Panama; several alate males and females collected from the same colony by W. M. Wheeler and I. Molino on 1923-iii-28, together with workers; the nest was of soft black earth beneath a tree. Holotype alate male, U.S.N.M. 26259. The same colony also contained one first-form queen and one male in a single chamber of the nest. The original also records measurements for the soldier of this species (total length 5.1—5.6 mm, head with mandibles 2.90—3.3 mm, left mandible 1.80 mm, head width 0.90—0.95 mm, etc.), but that passage lost its heading in the scan and its attribution cannot be confirmed, so no soldier section is given.
